name: Balcinrenone/dapagliflozin
summary: A once-daily fixed-dose capsule of balcinrenone (AZD9977), AstraZeneca's own mineralocorticoid receptor modulator, with dapagliflozin 10 mg. The lead Phase 3 is BalanceD-HF (NCT06307652): 3,850 patients with symptomatic heart failure of any ejection fraction, eGFR 20 to under 60, NT-proBNP above 300 and a heart failure event in the prior 6 months, randomised to balcinrenone/dapagliflozin 15/10 mg or 40/10 mg against dapagliflozin 10 mg alone; primary completion 2027-04-16. Price anchor: Kerendia (finerenone), the only non-steroidal MR agent on the US market and labelled in heart failure since July 2025, at $4,493 per Medicare Part D beneficiary in 2024. Uptake anchor: Kerendia's own CMS launch, 0.8% of its pool by its third full year, solved through the engine to 0.63% a year; Verquvo, the branded add-on labelled for the same post-event setting, solves to 0.74%. Not refused: balcinrenone is sold only inside the combination, but the combination is a product with its own revenue line; the part of it that displaces branded Farxiga until dapagliflozin's US substance patent lapses (2029-12-16, paediatric extension to 2030-06-16) is flagged, not netted. Heart failure incidence, blank in the book's epidemiology.csv, is carried on this asset as 752,400 new diagnoses a year: fee-for-service Medicare aged 65 and over in 2016 (Khera et al., JAMA Netw Open 2020, PMID 33095250), a lower bound on the national inflow, and eligible_pct applies to it unchanged. The SGLT2 class's uptake after a heart failure hospitalisation reads 0.069 a year for the class and about 0.023 for one brand, not 0.10, so 0.0063 stands with 0.023 as the case for higher.

therapy_mode.source: NCT06307652 interventions (book trial_interventions): balcinrenone/dapagliflozin 15 mg/10 mg or 40 mg/10 mg capsule once daily against dapagliflozin 10 mg, double-dummy; an event-driven outcomes study of about 38 months (Duke Clinical Research Institute study page, dcri.org/balanced-hf; Saudi FDA trial summary, sfda.gov.sa/en/node/1387762)
therapy_mode.note: Daily maintenance therapy for a chronic disease
therapy_mode.check: Book trial_interventions for NCT06307652: balcinrenone/dapagliflozin 15/10 mg or 40/10 mg with matching placebo for dapagliflozin 10 mg, against dapagliflozin 10 mg with matching placebo (double-dummy). Book trials table: primary outcome time to first CV death, HF hospitalisation or HF event without hospitalisation. DCRI study page (dcri.org/balanced-hf, via search): 'global, event-driven study lasting approximately 38 months'. Daily maintenance therapy, so chronic.

list_price_per_patient.source: lookup.py demand Kerendia: CMS Medicare Part D 2024, $396,302,773.23 over 88,208 beneficiaries = $4,493 per beneficiary
list_price_per_patient.note: Judgement on the comparator. Kerendia is the closest marketed product in mechanism and setting: the only non-steroidal MR agent in the US, approved on 2025-07-11 (openFDA, NDA215341 efficacy supplement 9, in the book's supplements table; Bayer announced it on 2025-07-14, bayer.com/en/us/news-stories/fda-approves-kerendia) for heart failure with LVEF 40% or above to cut CV death, HF hospitalisation and urgent HF visits, and labelled in CKD with type 2 diabetes. One brand price, not two: AstraZeneca's existing dapagliflozin combination, Xigduo XR, reads $4,366 per Part D beneficiary in 2024 against Farxiga's $4,168 (1.05x), and every branded heart failure product on file sits close by: Farxiga $4,168, Jardiance $4,496, Verquvo $4,465, Entresto $5,055 (lookup.py demand, Part D 2024). Case for higher: a price at the sum of the two agents, Kerendia plus Farxiga, would be $8,661. Kerendia's per-beneficiary figure is also still rising with its ramp ($1,493, $2,857, $4,239, $4,493 over 2021 to 2024), so a part-year effect remains. Case against the revenue as incremental: BalanceD-HF compares against dapagliflozin, so the patients switch from a dapagliflozin regimen. While Farxiga is branded, part of this revenue is a transfer from Farxiga's line, which the book models separately. The book's Orange Book rows put dapagliflozin's US substance patent 7,919,598 at 2029-12-16, with the paediatric extension to 2030-06-16. After that the combination protects dapagliflozin revenue that would otherwise go generic. Not netted here.
list_price_per_patient.check: Note only; value, unit and source unchanged. lookup.py demand Kerendia: Part D 2024 $396,302,773.23 / 88,208 beneficiaries = $4,492.8, so 0.004493 mm USD per patient-year; Kerendia rows are Part D only. Series $1,493, $2,857, $4,239, $4,493 (2021-2024) confirmed. Part D 2024 per beneficiary: Xigduo XR $4,366, Farxiga $4,168 (4,366/4,168 = 1.05), Jardiance $4,496, Verquvo $4,465, Entresto $5,055; Kerendia + Farxiga = $8,661. Kerendia label (book labels, Sep 2025): CKD with T2D and HF with LVEF >=40%. Correction: the note dated the HF approval 2025-07-14, which is Bayer's announcement date (search: 'On July 14, 2025, Bayer announced that the U.S. FDA approved'); openFDA records the FDA action on 2025-07-11 (NDA215341 supplement 9, efficacy). Orange Book rows (book exclusivities, asset 207): substance patent 7919598 to 2029-12-16, *PED to 2030-06-16. Labelled judgement with cases for higher and against.

gross_to_net_pct.source: house convention on a CMS Part D per-beneficiary price (backend/gross_to_net.py: halving lands at a median 96% of CMS's own negotiated net prices); Kerendia's rows in the book are Part D
gross_to_net_pct.note: Direction checked: 0.5 off list, so net is $2,246 per patient-year. Cross-check: the 2026 Medicare negotiated prices for the SGLT2 inhibitors this product sits beside are $178.50 (Farxiga) and $197.00 (Jardiance) per 30-day supply (book negotiated_prices, CMS maximum fair price file), $2,142 and $2,364 a year, which bracket this net
gross_to_net_pct.check: Anchor is Part D (Kerendia has no Part B rows), so the Part D convention applies: backend/gross_to_net.py PART_D_CONVENTION = 0.5, 'a median 96% of the negotiated price'. Direction right: 0.5 off list, net 0.004493 x 0.5 = $2,246.5. Book negotiated_prices (cms_mfp, effective 2026-01-01): Farxiga $178.50 and Jardiance $197.00 per 30 days; x12 = $2,142 and $2,364, which bracket the net.

discontinuation_pct.unit: share of treated stock stopping per year
discontinuation_pct.source: Greene SJ et al., 'Contemporary Guideline-Directed Medical Therapy for Heart Failure in the United States: The EMPACE Study', J Am Heart Assoc 2026;15(6):e044785, doi:10.1161/JAHA.125.044785, PMID 41804888 (Optum Market Clarity, 17,210 US patients hospitalised for heart failure, June 2020 to September 2023): 12-month discontinuation after initiation was 57% for mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists and 55% for SGLT2 inhibitors
discontinuation_pct.note: Judgement: the MRA rate is taken, not the SGLT2 inhibitor rate, because a patient who stops the MR component for potassium or kidney function stops the combination and returns to dapagliflozin alone. The setting matches BalanceD-HF's entry criterion, a recent heart failure event, and the data are US. Case against: a first-year rate applied to the whole stock every year overstates later-year stopping; 44.2% of steroidal MRA discontinuers restarted within a median 91 days in US claims (Richard EL et al., Pragmat Obs Res 2025;16:27-37, doi:10.2147/POR.S489791, PMID 40034401); and EVOLUTION HF pooled across Japan, Sweden and the US gives lower 12-month rates, 23.5% for dapagliflozin and 42.2% for MRAs (Savarese G et al., JACC Heart Fail 2023;11(1):1-14, doi:10.1016/j.jchf.2022.08.009, PMID 36202739). A single daily capsule may persist better than two pills
discontinuation_pct.check: PubMed 41804888 (Greene SJ et al., J Am Heart Assoc 2026;15(6):e044785, doi:10.1161/JAHA.125.044785) abstract: Optum Market Clarity June 2020-September 2023, 17,210 patients hospitalised for HF; 12-month discontinuation ARNI 62%, MRA 57%, SGLT2i 55%, beta blockers 51%. PubMed 40034401 (Richard EL, Pragmat Obs Res 2025;16:27-37): 44.2% of sMRA discontinuers restarted within a median 91 days. PubMed 36202739 (Savarese G, JACC Heart Fail 2023;11(1):1-14): pooled Japan, Sweden, US 12-month discontinuation 23.5% dapagliflozin, 42.2% MRAs. All as the note says. Labelled judgement with the case against.

forecast_start_year.source: NCT06307652 primary completion 2027-04-16, estimated (context file; book trials table); study expected to conclude in June 2027 (Duke Clinical Research Institute, dcri.org/balanced-hf)
forecast_start_year.note: Judgement on the filing and review timeline. No submission date is published (searched). A mid-2027 readout, a filing late in 2027 and a standard 12-month review for a new molecular entity put US approval in late 2028, so 2029 is the first full year. Case against: an event-driven study can run longer than its estimate, and a review that runs into 2029 makes 2030 the first full year
forecast_start_year.check: Book trials table NCT06307652: primary completion 2027-04-16 (estimated), start 2024-04-12, Recruiting, last update 2026-09-11. DCRI (dcri.org/balanced-hf, via search): 'expected to conclude in June 2027'. No submission date found in the book's AZN filing_sections (no balcinrenone text). Mid-2027 readout, filing late 2027, 12-month NME review gives late-2028 approval and 2029 as first full year. Labelled judgement with the case against.

exus_multiple.source: Lokelma FY2025 in the book's asset_revenue_regions (AZN 20-F 0001104659-26-019130, annual report table): US $301mm; Emerging Markets $129mm, Europe $129mm, Established ROW $139mm. 397 / 301 = 1.3189
exus_multiple.note: Judgement on the comparator. Lokelma is AstraZeneca's own branded cardio-renal specialty product, bought by the same cardiologists and nephrologists for the same patients on MR therapy, with no generic in its split. Entresto, the heart-failure-only brand, reads almost the same: Rest of world $4,463mm against US $3,285mm in FY2025 = 1.3586 (book asset_revenue_regions, Novartis 20-F 0001114448-26-000004). Case for higher: Farxiga, the dapagliflozin inside this product, reads 3.8555 (FY2025: US $1,730mm; Emerging Markets $3,324mm, Europe $2,941mm, Established ROW $405mm), because its US line is heavily rebated and its emerging-markets footprint is large. Other AZN seeds set that ratio aside as a legacy footprint, and so does this one
exus_multiple.check: Book asset_revenue_regions FY2025 (annual report table 0001104659-26-019130): Lokelma US $301mm; Emerging Markets $129mm, Europe $129mm, Established ROW $139mm; 397/301 = 1.31894. Entresto (0001114448-26-000004): Rest of world $4,463mm / US $3,285mm = 1.3586. Farxiga: (3,324 + 2,941 + 405)/1,730 = 3.8555. All as stated. Labelled comparator judgement.

economics_share.source: AstraZeneca is lead sponsor of NCT06307652, NCT07624305 and NCT07754331 (context file); balcinrenone carries AstraZeneca's own compound code AZD9977 and dapagliflozin is AstraZeneca's Farxiga; the book's asset_economics table holds no partner row for asset 1666

prevalence.source: carried by the book (epidemiology.csv: 7,400,000, American Heart Association 2025 statistics update)
prevalence.note: Carried by the book. The file's note says the pool is growing (8.7mm projected by 2030), so a flat figure understates the later years
prevalence.check: lookup.py pool 'Heart Failure': no asset carries a heart failure pool; epidemiology.csv carries prevalence 7,400,000 (AHA 2025 update, self-reported diagnosed adults 20+), with the note 'projected to 8.7mm by 2030 and 11.4mm by 2050'. Null is correct: the book fills it.

incidence.source: Khera R et al., 'Temporal Trends in Heart Failure Incidence Among Medicare Beneficiaries Across Risk Factor Strata, 2011 to 2016', JAMA Netw Open 2020;3(10):e2022190, doi:10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2020.22190, PMID 33095250, PMC7584929. Results: in CMS's 5% sample of fee-for-service Medicare beneficiaries aged 65 and over, continuously enrolled in Parts A and B and free of heart failure, 'the incidence of HF decreased ... to 26.5 cases per 1000 beneficiaries (n = 37 620) in 2016'; incident HF is at least one inpatient HF claim or two outpatient HF claims in separate quarters. Methods: 'for every 100 individuals enrolled in Medicare, 5 are entered into the Medicare 5% sample'. 37,620 x 20 = 752,400 new diagnoses a year in fee-for-service Medicare aged 65 and over
incidence.note: Population counted: new heart failure diagnoses in any setting, fee-for-service Medicare aged 65 and over, 2016. A lower bound on the national adult inflow: it leaves out Medicare Advantage enrollees and adults under 65, and 2016 is the latest year the paper counts (35.7 per 1,000 in 2011 falling to 26.5 in 2016). eligible_pct does not change. The engine passes incidence through the same eligible_pct as prevalence (forecast.patients_for_indication: incidence x eligible_pct x (1 + exus_multiple)), and this count measures what the book's 7.4mm measures, diagnosed heart failure, so the 0.17152 filter (event within 12 months, eGFR under 60) applies to it as it does to the prevalent pool. A first-hospitalisation count was the alternative and is not used: 2,634,645 incident heart failure hospitalisations in fee-for-service Medicare over 2014 to 2021, about 329,000 a year (J Card Fail 2025, doi:10.1016/j.cardfail.2025.12.006, PMID 41475614, abstract only). Those patients already meet the event criterion, so the engine would filter them for an event a second time (x 0.268), and one eligible_pct cannot be 0.64 for them and 0.17152 for the prevalent pool. It serves as a cross-check: about 44% of new diagnoses (329,000 over 752,400, different years) come through a hospitalisation, above the 26.8% event share applied, so the filter is conservative for new patients. The row is the asset's own, not the book's: epidemiology.csv leaves heart failure incidence blank, and assemble.py will copy this figure to any later heart failure asset. Engine consequence: untreated_carryover_pct is unset (1.0), so untreated eligible patients never leave by death. At the 0.0063 peak the engine's untreated eligible pool grows from 1.27mm to 2.45mm by year 10 (2038), against about 1.68mm at the same 0.17152 share of the book's own projected prevalence for 2038 (straight line from 8.7mm in 2030 to 11.4mm in 2050). The later-year pool is therefore overstated even with a lower-bound inflow. A carryover below 1.0 would correct it (1-year case fatality after a first acute decompensated heart failure admission is 29.5%, ARIC, PMID 24342763); not set here
incidence.check: Researcher left it null because epidemiology.csv leaves it blank. Replaced null with a study-based count seen in full text (PMC7584929): 37,620 incident HF in 2016 in the 5% fee-for-service sample aged 65+, x20 = 752,400. No national all-adult count found: PubMed title searches for US heart failure incidence returned rates only (Medicare 5% sample 19.9 per 1,000 person-years in 2017, PMC11611790; ARIC 11.6 per 1,000 aged 55+ for first ADHF admission, 2005-2009, PMID 24342763) or first-hospitalisation counts (PMID 41475614). The first-hospitalisation count was rejected for the engine basis reason in the note. Engine run (forecast.derive_new_patients, read-only): eligible inflow 752,400 x 0.17152 = 129,052 a year; untreated pool 1.27mm to 2.45mm by year index 9.

eligible_pct.source: Two filters from BalanceD-HF's entry criteria (Saudi FDA trial summary, sfda.gov.sa/en/node/1387762). (1) A heart failure event: 26.8% of 16,646 US patients with chronic HFrEF had a worsening event, a heart failure hospitalisation or IV diuretics, within 12 months ('Clinical and Economic Burden of Chronic Heart Failure and Reduced Ejection Fraction Following a Worsening Heart Failure Event', Adv Ther 2020, doi:10.1007/s12325-020-01456-1, PMID 32761552, PMC7444407; IBM MarketScan, accessed by Merck, index year 2016). (2) eGFR under 60: 234,332 of 365,494 heart failure hospitalisations (64%) in GWTG-HF, 2014 to 2019 (Patel RB et al., 'Kidney Function and Outcomes in Patients Hospitalized With Heart Failure', J Am Coll Cardiol 2021;78(4):330-343, doi:10.1016/j.jacc.2021.05.002, PMID 33989713). 0.268 x 0.64 = 0.17152, about 1.27mm of the book's 7.4mm
eligible_pct.note: The second share is measured among hospitalised patients, so it is already conditional on an event and the two multiply without an independence assumption. No ejection-fraction filter: the trial requires a recent LVEF reading but sets no cut-off. Case for lower: the trial requires the event within 6 months, not 12, and halving the first share gives 0.086. The 64% includes patients below eGFR 20, whom the trial excludes; the paper gives no count below 20, only a lower quartile of 34. The 26.8% comes from under-65 commercially insured HFrEF patients identified from claims, a sicker definition than the book's self-reported 7.4mm. Case for higher: older and HFpEF patients are hospitalised at least as often, and the label may drop the recent-event criterion, as the current US heart failure labels for Farxiga, Jardiance and Kerendia carry none. Verquvo's label does carry one (use following a heart failure hospitalisation or outpatient IV diuretics). Not applied: the trial also excludes current MRA users and requires NT-proBNP above 300 pg/mL, and a label would not restrict either
eligible_pct.check: PubMed 32761552 (Butler J et al., Adv Ther 2020;37(9):4015-4032): 'Of 16,646 patients with chronic HFrEF, 26.8% developed a WHFE' (HF hospitalisation or IV diuretics within 12 months; MarketScan commercial, under 65, index 2016). PubMed 33989713 (Patel RB et al., JACC 2021;78(4):330-343): 234,332 of 365,494 GWTG-HF hospitalisations (64%) had eGFR <60, median 51, IQR 34-72; 5% on dialysis. 0.268 x 0.64 = 0.17152; x 7.4mm = 1,269,248. Entry criteria confirmed via search (AstraZeneca trial page and site listings): eGFR >=20 to <60, NT-proBNP >300 pg/mL (>600 with AF), HF event within 6 months (hospitalisation or urgent visit), NYHA II-IV, any EF. Book labels: Farxiga, Jardiance and Kerendia HF indications carry no recent-event criterion; Verquvo's does ('following a hospitalization for heart failure or need for outpatient IV diuretics', EF <45%). The MRA-user exclusion was not seen, but it is not applied, so it does not move the value. Unchanged by the new incidence: that count is diagnosed HF on the prevalence's basis, so the same filter applies (see incidence). Labelled judgement with cases both ways.

penetration_peak_pct.unit: share of the eligible untreated pool per year at peak
penetration_peak_pct.source: Solved through the engine (forecast.derive_new_patients and treated_stock, read-only) from Kerendia's CMS Part D launch: 88,208 beneficiaries in 2024, its third full year (lookup.py demand Kerendia), over its CKD-with-type-2-diabetes pool of 11.07mm (the book's epidemiology.csv note on type 2 diabetes: 41% of 27.0mm adults, CDC), is 0.80% of the pool. With this asset's 0.57 discontinuation and Kerendia's fitted curve (k 1.82, midpoint 0.58), the engine needs a peak of 0.0063 to reach 88,208 in year index 2, and it reproduces 18,001 and 55,240 for 2022 and 2023 against actual 25,931 and 63,625. Incidence is left at zero in the solve; adding 41% of the book's type 2 diabetes incidence gives 0.0055
penetration_peak_pct.note: Judgement: the multiple is 1.0. Kerendia is the incumbent of the same prescribing decision: add a non-steroidal MR agent, with potassium monitoring, against generic spironolactone and eplerenone. Corroboration from the same setting: Verquvo, the branded add-on labelled for heart failure after a worsening event, had 11,127 Part D beneficiaries in 2024, its fourth year (lookup.py demand Verquvo). Over a pool of 7.4mm x 0.5 reduced ejection fraction (the book's epidemiology.csv note) x 26.8% with an event (PMID 32761552), the same solve gives 0.0074. Both numerators are Medicare Part D only, so both understate an all-payer capture. Case for higher: SGLT2 inhibitors were used by 12.0% of patients in the 12 months after a heart failure hospitalisation over June 2020 to September 2023 (EMPACE, PMID 41804888: 13% of HFrEF, 12% of HFmrEF and 9% of HFpEF, weighted by the cohort's 73/4/23 split). Solved as a year-3 treated stock that needs a peak of 0.10, but the reading overstates it twice. The 12.0% includes the 5.5% already on an SGLT2 inhibitor before the admission (5%, 7% and 7%), so new starts were 6.5 points, 6.9% of those not on one. And it is a one-year capture of a post-event cohort, which is what this peak measures, not a stock three years into a launch. The class figure is therefore 0.069, and it spans two heart failure brands: Farxiga held 32.7% of SGLT2 inhibitor Part D beneficiaries in 2024 (1,269,216 of 3,879,658 across Farxiga, Jardiance, Invokana and Steglatro, lookup.py demand), which puts one brand at about 0.023, 3.6 times this value. In the engine with this asset's incidence, year 5 treated US patients are about 19,000 at 0.0063, 67,000 at 0.023 and 252,000 at 0.10; the last is a fifth of Farxiga's whole 2024 Part D base and 2.9 times Kerendia's year-3 count. 0.0063 matches what the two single-brand incumbents measurably reached (Kerendia 0.80% of its pool by year 3; Verquvo 11,127 in year 4, 1.1% of its post-event pool) and stays, with 0.023 as the case for higher. Entresto held 795,291 Part D beneficiaries in 2024, 10.7% of the whole 7.4mm. AstraZeneca can also switch patients from its own Farxiga (1.27mm Part D beneficiaries in 2024, all indications) to one capsule, a channel Bayer did not have for Kerendia. Case for lower: finerenone will have been labelled in heart failure for three years by launch, and the MR component faces generic steroidal MRAs
penetration_peak_pct.check: Note only; value 0.0063 and source unchanged. Recomputed with backend/forecast.py (read-only): pool 0.41 x 27.0mm = 11.07mm, incidence 0, discontinuation 0.57, k 1.82, midpoint 0.58; the peak that puts treated stock at 88,208 in year index 2 is 0.006299, reproducing 18,001 and 55,240 (actual 25,931 and 63,625). With 41% of T2D incidence (0.41 x 1,387,500): 0.00553. Verquvo check: pool 7.4mm x 0.5 x 0.268 = 991,600, 11,127 at year index 3 (2024 as its fourth year) gives 0.00739. 88,208/11.07mm = 0.797%; Entresto 795,291/7.4mm = 10.7%. EMPACE figures confirmed in the PubMed abstract (13/12/9% after, 5/7/7% before, 73/4/23 split); weighted after 12.04%, before 5.54%. The researcher's 0.10 reproduces (stock = 12% of the 1.27mm eligible pool at year index 2 needs 0.1021), but it treats a one-year use share, prior users included, as a year-3 stock. Corrected reading: 0.069 for the class, about 0.023 for one brand at Farxiga's 32.7% Part D share. Engine runs with incidence 752,400 x 0.17152: year-5 US treated stock 19.0k (0.0063), 66.9k (0.023), 182.5k (0.069), 251.9k (0.1021). The value is a labelled judgement on a named incumbent with confirmed inputs, so it is kept.

ramp_steepness.source: Kerendia's CMS Part D beneficiaries, 1,908 (2021, a part year), 25,931, 63,625, 88,208 (2022 to 2024) (lookup.py demand Kerendia), least-squares logistic fit with 2022, the first full year, as index 0: plateau 94,500, k 1.82, midpoint 0.58 years; fitted 5,044, 24,395, 64,478, 87,871
ramp_steepness.note: Measured on the closest-mechanism launch in the book; no heart failure pipeline seed exists to reuse. Case against: four points, one a part year, pin the plateau poorly, and the series ends before Kerendia's July 2025 heart failure label, so the fit may read as saturation what was a pause. The book's other measured launches are slower: Enhertu k 1.08, midpoint 2.2 (ABBV-1480 and camizestrant seeds) and Zeposia k 1.005, midpoint 2.15 (tulisokibart seed)
ramp_steepness.check: Kerendia Part D beneficiaries 1,908, 25,931, 63,625, 88,208 (2021-2024), lookup.py demand. Researcher's curve (94,500, k 1.82, midpoint 0.58, 2022 = index 0) gives 5,044, 24,393, 64,479, 87,869. My least-squares grid fit gives plateau 94,250, k 1.84, midpoint 0.58 (4,882, 24,122, 64,479, 87,811), the same curve to within the grid step. Labelled, with the four-point, pre-HF-label case against.

ramp_midpoint_year.source: as ramp_steepness (Kerendia's CMS Part D fit)
ramp_midpoint_year.note: Half of peak penetration in the first full year. The penetration solve above uses this same curve, so the two move together: changing the curve without re-solving the peak breaks the anchor
ramp_midpoint_year.check: Same fit as ramp_steepness: midpoint 0.58 years from 2022 in both fits. The peak solve uses this curve, as the note says.
